usage: Save as clean_workbook.py after operator review. Requires Python 3.10+ and an installed openpyxl package. Run: python clean_workbook.py < input.json > output.json. Alternatively call clean_workbook(payload). Input is one contract object; output contains only workbook_b64. No network or subprocess calls occur. The tool processes all populated Data records and uses row_bound as a record-count ceiling. IDs retain their original cell representation, including Unicode and leading zeros. Duplicate detection precedes numeric validation. Blank numbers become zero; malformed numbers, booleans, errors and numeric-input formulas cause row removal. Dates accept Excel dates/serials, ISO timestamps and the explicit formats in source; ambiguous slash dates use month/day first, blank dates remain blank, and unrecognized dates raise an error. Amount and Total formulas receive calculated numeric caches directly in XLSX XML. Other sheets retain their original XML and cached values, except Summary A1/B1. This is not a general formula recalculation engine: unrelated formula caches are preserved and Excel is instructed to recalculate on opening. Macros and external relationships are rejected. Source has not been executed or tested. task and variation are metadata; cleaning behavior is fixed by the contract.
